ios.desc:
Know what's due. Know what you've taken.

Dosis is a private medication tracker designed by a pharmacist. Open Today to see upcoming doses, doses past their scheduled time that have not been logged, and what you've already recorded. Mark Taken or Skipped, see when a taken dose was recorded, and undo accidental entries.

Medication information stays on your device and is never uploaded to a Dosis server. No account. No ads.

Add medications, supplements, or injections, set daily, weekly, every-few-days, or on/off cycle schedules with custom daily times, and mark doses in seconds. Log doses from your Apple Watch, and use Dosis on iPhone and iPad.

Following a weekly GLP-1 medication routine? Choose your injection day and time, get a reminder, rotate injection sites, and keep your dose history alongside the rest of your medications.

Start free with two active medications, the Today screen, schedules, reminders, and dose logging. Optional treatment dates, notes, and pharmacy details can be added later.

With Dosis Premium, unlock unlimited medications, supply tools, adherence insights, and PDF medication lists that are easy to share with a healthcare professional.

Key features:
- Today view with upcoming, unlogged, and recorded doses
- Explicit Taken, Skipped, and Undo actions
- Daily, weekly, and Every X Days medication schedules
- Apple Watch app for logging doses from your wrist
- iPhone and iPad support
- Weekly injection reminders by day and time
- Injection site rotation with next-site suggestions
- Repeat Until Logged follow-up reminders
- On/off cycles and doses every few hours
- Medication photos and expiration dates
- Fast dose check-ins with compact history grids
- Supply counts that decrease by the units used per dose
- Week and Month adherence summaries with Taken, Skipped, Not logged, and Upcoming counts
- Dated dose history with tap-to-view details
- Shareable PDF medication reports
- No account, no ads, and no developer collection of medication data

Dosis supports medication tracking but does not provide medical advice, prescribe treatment, or replace guidance from your healthcare professional.
